# noqa-justification (KNQ001)

**noqa justification**

This rule is enabled by default.

## What it does

Requires every `# noqa` comment to carry a reason. The reason is any text after the directive in the same comment (leading `#`, `-` and `:` are ignored, but it needs at least one letter or digit). The `# noqa: CODE  # reason` form is recommended because it reads the same to every tool that parses the comment. Only real comments count: `# noqa` inside a string literal is not flagged.

## Why is this bad?

A bare suppression hides a violation without recording why that is fine. Months later nobody knows whether it is still needed or safe to remove. A short reason makes the exception reviewable.

## Example

```python
from os.path import join   # noqa: KIS001
value = compute()          # noqa
```

Use instead:

```python
from os.path import join   # noqa: KIS001  # re-exported for plugins
value = compute()          # noqa: KPT010 - generated code
```

## Suppressing and fixing

This rule cannot be suppressed with `# noqa` (not even `# noqa: KNQ001`), and `--ignore-noqa` does not affect it. Turn it off with `ignore` or `per-file-ignores` instead. It is not fixable: `konform check --add-noqa` never targets it, and appends reasonless comments that this rule then flags until a reason is added.

## Options

Configured in `[tool.konform.lint.noqa-justification]`.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `level` | `"warning" \| "error"` | `"error"` | Severity of violations. Set `warning` to roll the rule out gradually. |

## Suppression

```python
x = 1  # noqa: KNQ001
x = 1  # noqa: KNQ  (every KNQ* rule)
```
